transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like I’m just a really bad employee and a terrible homeowner, and I deserve to lose everything I’ve worked so hard for. It's just... well, like with the house, the gutters have been overflowing every time it rains lately. It makes this awful splashing sound against the siding. I meant to buy one of those extension ladders from Home Depot, the tall aluminum ones? But then I got distracted because they had a huge clearance event on patio furniture, which is ridiculous anyway because I don't even have a patio. I just have this small wooden deck in the back that desperately needs restaining. I'm pretty sure the people who lived there before me used a really cheap sealant, and now the wood is starting to splinter on the edges, especially near the stairs... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, I just feel like everything is my fault.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge about things that are happening or might happen?

No, I don't really feel nervous or on edge about things. I don't sit around worrying about what's going to happen, really. Actually, my manager at work—I'm a business operations specialist—he asked me the other day if I was anxious about the new Q3 software rollout. We're switching to this new cloud-based inventory system, which honestly is a complete mess because the vendor didn't even map the data fields correctly. I spent like three hours on Tuesday just trying to align the columns in Excel. And Excel has been crashing on me constantly lately anyway. I think it's because my work laptop is from like 2019 and the fan makes this incredibly loud whirring sound whenever I open more than two tabs. I tried blowing dust out of the vents with one of those compressed air cans, but it just made my fingers really cold and the air smelled kind of weird... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, being on edge. No, I don't really get nervous like that.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

I wouldn't really say I feel sad, exactly. Not like... crying all the time or anything. Like I said before, I just feel like everything is my fault, but sad... no, I don't think so. I still get up and make my coffee every morning. I've been using a French press lately because my regular coffee maker broke. The glass carafe just shattered in the sink while I was washing it last month. It was actually super dangerous, there were tiny shards of glass everywhere, even stuck in the grout of the countertop tiles. I had to use a flashlight and a piece of wet bread to pick up all the little invisible pieces. I saw that trick on a lifehack video on YouTube once. I end up watching a lot of YouTube, honestly, mostly those videos where they restore old rusty tools? It's weirdly satisfying watching them soak old wrenches in vinegar for days and then scrub them down until they shine. I don't even own any tools, really, except a basic hammer and a cheap screwdriver set where the plastic handle is completely cracking off... wait, what were we talking about? Oh. Sadness. Yeah, no, I don't really feel sad most of the time.
Do you find pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. I used to do a lot, actually. I used to plan all these weekend brunches, and I'd go hiking, and even sign up for those professional networking events for work. I also used to paint a lot in my spare room. But lately... I don't know, all of those things just feel like tasks I’m pretending to care about. Especially the painting. I haven't touched my canvases in months. I actually bought this really expensive easel online right before I stopped, one of those solid beechwood ones that adjusts to different angles? But it arrived missing a wingnut for the main bracket. I tried to find a replacement at the hardware store, but the threading was metric, and the guy working in the fastener aisle—he had this huge bushy mustache that kept twitching when he talked—he told me I'd have to order a special part from Germany. Which is completely ridiculous for a piece of metal the size of a dime. I ended up just using a heavy-duty zip tie to hold it together, but now it wobbles every time the AC turns on. The AC vents in that spare room are super dusty anyway, I really need to get up there and change the filters, but the ceilings are vaulted so I'd need that extension ladder I never bought... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I just feel like I'm going through the motions with all that stuff now.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

My appetite has been all over the place, honestly. Mostly I just skip real meals during the day and I've been living on coffee, toast, and whatever is easiest. Speaking of toast, my toaster has been acting up lately. The lever won't stay down unless I wedge a butter knife in the side, which I know is probably a terrible fire hazard. My dad used to yell at me for doing stuff like that when I was a kid. He was an electrician, actually, so he was always super paranoid about wiring and appliances. He used to spend his weekends rewiring our entire garage just for fun. He had this massive pegboard with every single tool outlined in black Sharpie so you knew exactly where it went. I tried doing that in my kitchen once for my spatulas and cooking spoons, but the marker bled into the drywall and it just looked like a giant, messy inkblot test. I ended up having to paint over the whole wall with this color the hardware store called "Tuscan Sunrise," but it really just looked like a faded traffic cone when the afternoon light hit it... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, weight. Um, yeah, I've noticed my clothes are a lot looser lately because of the whole not eating real meals thing.
Do you still find any activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy to be pleasurable now?

I think... I think you already asked me that, didn't you? About enjoying things? But yeah, like I was saying, no, not really. I used to be so organized with my weekends. I'd plan all these elaborate brunches for my friends, and I’d go hiking out at the state park, and I’d even sign up for those professional networking events for work just to stay sharp. And I used to paint a lot in that spare room. But now... I don't know, it all just feels like a chore. Like they're just tasks I'm pretending to care about, you know? Especially the brunches. I used to make this incredible quiche with gruyere and spinach. The trick is to blind-bake the crust first with pie weights, otherwise the bottom gets completely soggy from the egg mixture. I actually lost my ceramic pie weights last time I moved. They came in this little canvas drawstring bag, and I think it accidentally got packed into a box of winter coats that I ended up donating to Goodwill. Which is annoying, because I really liked those coats, especially this one long wool trench coat I had. It was camel-colored and had these really deep pockets that were perfect for keeping my hands warm when I had to take the train into the city for work. The train always smelled like stale coffee and wet newspaper, but I kind of liked the commute because I could listen to podcasts. I used to listen to this one about unsolved historical mysteries, like the Roanoke colony and stuff... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, hobbies. Yeah, like I said, I just don't really care about any of that stuff anymore. It's all just... exhausting to even think about.
Do you feel like you're worthless or that you have no value as a person?

Yeah, actually, that's kind of... that's a big part of why I came in. I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is entirely my fault. Like I'm just a fundamentally bad employee, and a terrible homeowner, and I just deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. Speaking of the house, I got this notice from the HOA last week about the paint on my mailbox fading. They have these incredibly specific rules about what shade of black you're allowed to use—it has to be "Onyx Matte," not "Charcoal" or "Midnight." The HOA president is this retired guy, Gary, who literally walks around the neighborhood with a clipboard and a color swatch at, like, 6 AM. I saw him once when I was taking the trash out early because the garbage truck always comes on Tuesdays before I even wake up. Our garbage guys are actually really nice, though. One of them found my Amazon package that had blown into the street during a storm and put it on my porch. It was just a pack of replacement heads for my electric toothbrush, but still, it was nice of him. I've been trying to use the soft bristle ones because my dentist told me I brush too hard and I'm receding my gums. She said I need to hold the brush with just two fingers to reduce the pressure, but it feels so awkward, like I'm trying to write with my non-dominant hand... wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, feeling worthless. Yeah, I just feel like I'm failing at everything, like I'm just a bad person who doesn't deserve any of the good things I have.
Do you feel depressed most of the time?

Um, I don't really know if it's *most* of the time, honestly. It's just hard to keep track of time lately. Actually, the wall clock in my home office has been stuck at 3:15 for like a month because I keep forgetting to buy AA batteries. I finally went to Walgreens to get some last night, but they completely rearranged the aisles. I don't know why stores do that. You get so used to the batteries being right by the photo counter, and then suddenly they're all the way in the back next to the seasonal candy. They already had all this Valentine's Day chocolate out, which is crazy because it's not even close to February. I ended up buying a bag of those little conversation hearts anyway, even though they taste exactly like chalk. My mom used to put those in my lunchbox when I was in elementary school. She'd write little notes on my napkins, too, usually just reminding me to eat my carrots. I never did, though. I always traded my carrots for this kid Jeremy's fruit snacks. Jeremy had this intense obsession with dinosaurs, like he could name every single era—the Jurassic, the Cretaceous, all of it. He even had this green backpack that had plush dinosaur spikes running all the way down the center zipper. I kind of wonder what happened to him, if he became a paleontologist or something... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, about being depressed. Um, yeah, I'm just not really sure how to measure it. I just feel down a lot, but I don't know if I'd say it's most of the time.
Do you often feel guilty about things that you've done or haven't done?

I think... wait, didn't I just say something about that? About feeling like everything is my fault? Because yeah, that's really the main reason I even made this appointment. I just have this constant, heavy feeling that I'm a terrible employee, and a terrible homeowner, and that I completely deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. Like I'm just fundamentally failing at life. Which reminds me, I actually got a letter from the city yesterday about my property taxes, and the envelope had this weird sort of wax seal on it, which I thought was so strange for a government document. It looked like one of those fancy wedding invitations you get where people hire a calligrapher. My cousin Sarah did that for her wedding last year. She got married in this beautiful converted barn up in Vermont, and they had a hot cocoa bar because it was October and kind of chilly. I remember trying to find a dress for it, and I ordered like six different ones online because I couldn't decide on the color. I ended up wearing this forest green wrap dress, but the fabric was that really static-y kind of polyester, so it kept clinging to my tights all night. I had to keep going into the bathroom to rub lotion on my legs to stop the static. The bathroom at that venue had these really intricate vintage brass faucets that looked like swans... wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling guilty. Yeah, like I said before, I just feel like everything going wrong is my fault and I'm just a bad person.
How long have you been feeling like everything is your fault?

Well, I guess... the feeling down and just not really caring about anything anymore, that's been going on for about two years and one month, I think. It started right around the time I bought my car, actually. It's a Honda Civic, silver, which I thought would be really practical because silver doesn't show dirt as much as black or white. But honestly, the birds in my neighborhood seem to specifically target it anyway. There's this massive oak tree right over my driveway, and in the fall, it drops these huge acorns that sound like hail when they hit the roof. I actually had to get a dent repaired on the hood last spring. The auto body shop was right next to this amazing little authentic Mexican bakery. While I was waiting for the estimate, I went in and got this pan dulce—the pink ones that look like seashells? Conchas, I think they're called. The lady working there was so sweet, she gave me an extra one for free because it was near closing time. She had on this beautiful apron embroidered with all these bright sunflowers. My grandmother used to grow sunflowers along the side of her garage. They got so tall they practically reached the roof, and the heads were as big as dinner plates. We used to harvest the seeds and roast them in the oven with just a little bit of sea salt... um, wait. What did you ask me? Oh, right, how long I've felt like this. Yeah, about two years and a month.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy doing?

Um, I don't know. I used to do a lot. Like, I used to plan all these brunches, and I'd paint in my spare room... actually, I painted the walls of that spare room this really specific sage green. I had to go to Home Depot like four times to get the right shade because the fluorescent lighting in the store completely changes how the swatches look. The guy working in the paint department was super helpful, though. His name tag said Arthur, and he told me he was retiring in two weeks to move to Florida. He showed me pictures of this little condo he bought in Boca Raton. It had this screened-in porch with a ceiling fan, which seems really necessary for the humidity down there. I've only been to Florida once, when I was like ten, and we went to Disney World. I remember I dropped my ice cream cone right on Main Street, and this guy in a Goofy costume came over and pretended to cry about it with me. It was funny, but I was still really devastated about the ice cream. It was mint chocolate chip, which is still my favorite... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, if I still enjoy activities. Right. Well, like I was saying, I used to do all that—paint in the spare room, host brunches, go hiking, and even sign up for networking events for my career. But now... honestly, no. All those things just feel like tasks I’m pretending to care about.
Are there any small pleasures in life that you still look forward to?

I mean... small pleasures? Not really. Like I just said, I used to do all these things. I'd plan those brunches with my friends, and I had my painting in the spare room, and I'd go hiking on the weekends... I even used to sign up for all these networking events for work. I bought this really nice blazer for one of them, actually. It was navy blue with these gold buttons, kind of nautical looking. I got it on sale at Macy's because it was missing one of the buttons on the sleeve, but I figured I could just take the other ones off or replace them all. I ended up finding these vintage brass buttons at a flea market that looked exactly like the ones on my grandfather's old naval uniform. He was in the Navy for like twenty years, stationed all over the place. He used to send us postcards from Japan with these beautiful cherry blossoms on them. I always wanted to go to Japan in the spring to see the blossoms in person. They have these festivals where people just sit under the trees and drink tea and eat... um, wait. What were we talking about? Oh, small pleasures. Right. No, I don't look forward to anything anymore. Even those things I used to do, like the brunches and the hiking and the networking... they all just feel like chores now. Like I'm just going through the motions and pretending to care about them, but I don't.
Do you feel a persistent feeling of emptiness inside?

Emptiness? Um... I'm not really sure if empty is the right word. I don't think I feel empty. Actually, speaking of empty, I was cleaning out my work tote the other day because I was looking for my office ID badge, and I realized the bottom zipper compartment was completely empty except for this one really nice pen I thought I had lost months ago. It’s this heavy silver fountain pen a coworker brought back for me from Italy. She went to Rome and Florence for her honeymoon. She brought back all these amazing photos, and she said the pasta there was just incredible. 

I actually tried making homemade pasta from scratch after she told me about it. I bought the little metal crank machine and everything. It was a complete disaster, honestly. I got flour all over the kitchen floor, and my cat walked right through it and tracked little white paw prints all the way down the hallway and onto my living room rug. It's this dark red Persian-style rug, so getting fine flour out of those fibers was just... a total nightmare. I had to go rent one of those heavy carpet cleaners from the grocery store, the ones that are always slightly wet and smell kind of like industrial soap... um, wait. Sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, emptiness. Right. No, I don't think I have a feeling of emptiness inside. I don't really know how to describe it, but not empty.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep patterns recently?

Sleep? Um, yeah. It's been pretty bad. Most nights I just lie awake for hours, just listening to the house settle. You know how old houses make those weird popping noises? My house was built in the fifties, so it has all these original hardwood floors that creak if you even look at them wrong. I actually tried to fix one of the squeakiest floorboards in the hallway last weekend. I watched this whole YouTube tutorial about using baby powder or talcum powder to lubricate the joints between the wood. I ended up buying this huge bottle of baby powder at CVS, but the cashier accidentally double-scanned it, so I had to wait for a manager to come do an override. The manager was this really young guy who looked like he was maybe eighteen, and he was trying to figure out the register system while chewing this really bright blue gum. It smelled exactly like that blue raspberry cotton candy you get at the fair. I haven't been to a state fair in years. The last time I went, I won this giant stuffed banana with dreadlocks playing the ring toss... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Sleep. Yeah, so I lie awake listening to the house, and then even when I finally drift off, I wake up around three or four in the morning. And then I just can't get back to sleep before I have to log on for work. It's exhausting.
How long have you been feeling this way, with everything seeming to be your fault and lacking interest in activities?

How long? Um, let me think... It started right around the time I bought my current car, I think. I got this used silver sedan, and the dealership I went to was right off the interstate. The guy who sold it to me was wearing this really overpowering cologne. It smelled exactly like pine needles and cheap aftershave, like he just bathed in it before his shift. He kept trying to upsell me on these heavy-duty all-weather floor mats, which I actually ended up getting anyway because I spill coffee in my car constantly on my way to the office. 

I have this metal travel mug that's supposed to be completely leak-proof, but the rubber seal on the lid is totally shot. I bought it at this little independent coffee shop downtown, the one that roasts their own beans in the back window. They make this incredible dark roast that has these notes of dark chocolate and toasted almonds... um, wait. Sorry, I completely lost my train of thought again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, how long I've been feeling like this. Yeah, the depression and just... losing interest in everything. It's been with me for about two years and one month now.
Have you experienced any significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities for more than two weeks?

Loss of interest? Um, yeah. Definitely. I used to do a lot, actually. I'd plan these big Sunday brunches, paint in the spare room, go hiking on the weekends, and I used to sign up for all these professional networking events. Actually, the last networking event I went to was at this hotel downtown, the one with the huge glass revolving doors? I always get so anxious in revolving doors because I feel like I'm going to time my step wrong and get my shoe stuck. 

My cousin actually got stuck in one at a mall when we were kids. They had to call the fire department to pry the glass back. One of the firefighters let her wear his helmet, which was way too big for her, and she wouldn't take it off for the rest of the day. We went to get ice cream after, and she was just sitting in the booth eating mint chocolate chip with this massive yellow helmet on. I hate mint chocolate chip, honestly. It just tastes like cold toothpaste with chocolate chunks in it. I don't get why people like it, it completely ruins the chocolate... um, wait. Sorry. What was the question again? Oh, right, losing interest in things. Yeah. So, all those things I mentioned—the brunches, the painting, the hiking, the events—now they just feel like tasks I’m pretending to care about. It's been way longer than two weeks.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past two years?

Weight? Um, yeah, I guess so. My appetite has been all over the place lately. I mostly just skip real meals during the day now. I actually used to meal prep every Sunday. I had this whole system with these glass containers I bought online. They had these little snap-on lids with silicone seals that were supposed to be completely airtight, but one of them melted in the dishwasher. 

My dishwasher has this weird quirk where the bottom rack gets incredibly hot, like way hotter than it should. I tried to call a repair guy about it, but the company I used had this automated phone menu that just kept looping me back to the main menu. I was on hold for like forty-five minutes listening to this awful elevator music. It was this really tinny jazz cover of "Girl from Ipanema." My dad used to play a lot of jazz when I was growing up. He had this massive record collection that he kept alphabetized, and if you ever put a record back in the wrong sleeve, he'd know immediately. He had this one Miles Davis album that... wait. Sorry. What were we talking about? 

Oh, right, weight loss. Yeah. So, like I was saying, I skip meals and mostly just live on coffee and toast, or whatever is easiest to grab. I haven't actually weighed myself, but I've definitely noticed my clothes are getting a lot looser.
Have you had any periods of at least two weeks where you felt better and were interested in activities?

Periods where I felt better? Um, let me think... I mean, there was a stretch... yeah, there was a stretch of several weeks where my mood wasn't quite as heavy. I was actually getting through my work at the office a lot more normally. My office is in this big corporate park, and they just redesigned the whole layout to be an open floor plan. It's supposed to encourage collaboration or whatever, but it just means you can hear every single phone conversation happening on the entire floor. 

The guy who sits at the desk across from me, Kevin, he clicks his pen constantly when he's on conference calls. Click-click, click-click, for like an hour straight. I tried to buy him one of those silent fidget toys to take the hint, but I couldn't find the right one on Amazon. Amazon has so many knock-off brands now, it's impossible to tell what's actually good quality. I ordered a phone charger last month that claimed it was fast-charging, but it actually drains my battery if I use the phone while it's plugged in. It has this really bright blue LED light on it that lights up my whole bedroom at night, so I had to cover it with electrical tape. I have this roll of black electrical tape that I've had since college... um, wait. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Sorry, what was the question? 

Oh, right, feeling better. Yeah, so there were those few weeks where work was easier and the depression wasn't as bad. But even during that time, I was still hearing the voice whispering near the air vents, and I was still completely convinced that the mortgage company and my coworkers were monitoring everything I did. So the mood lifted a bit, but that other stuff never went away.
Have you experienced any physical symptoms like headaches or muscle aches alongside your feelings of worthlessness and loss of interest in activities?

Physical symptoms? Like headaches? Um, no, I don't really get headaches. Or muscle aches, not really. I mean, my neck gets stiff sometimes, but I think that's just from my chair at work. It's one of those ergonomic ones that's supposed to be good for your posture, but it has this weird lumbar support thing that digs right into my lower back. I tried adjusting it, but the knob is completely stuck. I actually brought in some WD-40 from home to try and loosen it. 

I keep a can of WD-40 under my kitchen sink because the hinges on my cabinet doors squeak so loudly. My apartment building is pretty old, so everything squeaks. The floorboards in the hallway sound like someone is walking right behind you even when you're alone. The landlord said he was going to fix it before winter, but he never did. He's this guy who wears a lot of cologne, like, way too much. You can smell him in the lobby for like an hour after he leaves. It smells like pine needles and cheap aftershave. It always reminds me of those little tree air fresheners people hang in their cars. My dad used to have a green one in his old station wagon, and we'd drive to the lake in the summer and... wait, sorry. I got distracted again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, headaches and muscle aches. No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. Just the usual stuff I was talking about before.

Have you had at least five of the following symptoms nearly every day for the past two weeks: depressed mood, markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities, significant weight loss or gain, insomnia or hypersomnia, psychomotor agitation or retardation, fatigue or loss of energy, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, diminished ability to think or concentrate, or recurrent thoughts of death?

Five of those? Um, yeah, definitely the depressed mood and not enjoying anything anymore. And the insomnia, for sure. My sleep has been so terrible lately that I actually just bought one of those shredded memory foam pillows online to see if it would help. It came vacuum-sealed in this tiny plastic tube, and when you cut the plastic, it expands to like five times its size. But it had this horrible chemical smell—off-gassing, I think they call it. 

I tried leaving it out on my balcony to air out, but my balcony faces this alley where the garbage trucks come at like four in the morning. The noise is unbelievable. The trucks have that really loud reverse beeping sound, and it just echoes off the brick walls of the building next door. There's this one stray cat that always hangs out by the dumpsters there. It's an orange tabby, but it's missing half of its left ear. I tried to leave some canned tuna out for it once, but a raccoon got to it first. Raccoons have those creepy little human hands, and they just... um, wait. Sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. What was the list you were reading?

Oh, the symptoms, right. Yeah, I have most of those on your list. Really, looking back, the low mood and the total loss of interest... they've been there for almost the whole time since this all started. Like I was saying earlier, there were those brief periods where I could function a little better and get through work, but otherwise, that heavy, empty feeling is just always there.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
